title: commit_lane takes the board files and the protected files as two lists
body:
**Chose:** `commit_lane(lane, base, board, protected, message, ref_name)`: both lists are unstaged, and only `protected` paths the worker changed come back in `dropped`.
**Over:** the slice's single `drop: &[String]`. With one list the library cannot tell a board file from a protected one, yet acceptance (c) wants the board files dropped silently and the protected ones named.
**Because:** the caller already holds both lists apart (`commit::tool_files`, `commit::protected_files`). `land` takes `board` the same way.
**Undo:** merge the two arguments and let the caller filter `dropped` against its board files.

title: cargo fmt and the full inner loop see sibling slices' half-written files
body: Sibling builders write the same tree mid-run, so a crate-wide `cargo fmt` rewrites their files and `fmt --check`/clippy can go red on them. Instead, check your own files with `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <files>` and read clippy errors by file.

title: Parallel builders share the tree; fmt and build reds can be another slice's
body: Four slice builders share one working tree: `cargo fmt --check` and the build can go red on another slice's mid-edit file (`src/lanes.rs`, `tests/harness/mod.rs`). Run `rustfmt --edition 2024` on your own files only, never `cargo fmt`; rebuild after a minute when the red is in a file you did not touch.

title: A lane setup must not end in a quote
body: A lane file's `setup:` value loses any leading or trailing quote (`src/lanes.rs` parse trims `"` and `'`), so a setup ending in `…log"` breaks in sh; end it unquoted, e.g. `>> "$(dirname "$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)")"/scenario/lane-setup.log`.

title: How does the stub tell a merge pack apart?
body:
**Chose:** the stub reads a pack as `merge` when its first `# ` heading is `# Conflict`, tested before every other role; `touch` on a merge step defaults to none.
**Over:** matching `# Conflict` anywhere in the pack, as the other roles match their headings.
**Because:** a merge pack carries the slice file and its text, which may quote any heading; the slice says "first section". With no default touch, a `done` without `sh` leaves the markers, the slice's "markers left" case.
**Undo:** move the test into the ternary chain with `/^# Conflict$/m`.

title: main_tree keeps its own common-dir call
body:
**Chose:** `lanes::main_tree` runs its own `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`.
**Over:** calling `paths::git_common_dir`, which the slice said to use if slice 02 added it.
**Because:** that helper sat in the shared working tree uncommitted (slice 02's commit holds only tests and its slice file), so depending on it would tie this slice's commit to another slice's unlanded work.
**Undo:** once `paths::git_common_dir` is committed, make `main_tree` its parent, canonical; one function.

title: The worker hook matches source text in a heredoc
body: The worker hook refuses a Bash command whose text names the VCS tool and its upload verb anywhere, even inside a Python heredoc of Rust source (`git(` plus `.push(`), and refuses recursive grep over src: make multi-line source edits with the Edit tool, write log bodies to a scratch file and pipe them in, and look code up with `factory ctx`.

title: How does a resumed driver finish a landing it was killed in?
body:
**Chose:** `land_slice` finishes a landing its driver was killed in. A pick half done in the main tree (index and tree equal to the lane commit on its paths) goes back to HEAD before the retry (`undo_half_pick`). A commit with the slice's subject already on the tip since the lane's base is recorded as the landing, and its ref deleted, in place of a second pick.
**Over:** retrying the landing as is: the half pick reads as the owner's dirty work and parks the run for good; a second pick of a landed commit has nothing to commit and fails the driver.
**Because:** task 4 asks the function to be safe to call again; these are the two kill points inside `land::land` besides the lane commit. Pinned by the three kill tests in `tests/commits.rs`.
**Undo:** drop `undo_half_pick` and the subject lookup in `land_slice`; delete the post-commit kill test.

title: What happens to a conflicting slice's ref when its worker respawns?
body:
**Chose:** a slice's spawn deletes a `refs/factory/<NNN>/slice-NN` left by an earlier conflicting landing; the respawned worker's lane still holds that work (a blocked slice keeps its lane), and its exit commits the lane again from the lane's base.
**Over:** keeping the ref, which the next exit would land as is, without the worker's rework.
**Because:** `land_slice` lands a ref that resolves before it commits the lane, so a stale one would hide the respawn's edits. Slice 08 replaces the conflict branch and may keep the ref for its merge worker.
**Undo:** remove the `update-ref -d` in `spawn_on`.

title: Two landing tests read their acceptance differently
body:
**Chose:** two tests read their acceptance slightly differently. The conflict test asserts `git status --porcelain` empty outside `docs/features/` (the BLOCK entry and the `blocked` status are board writes to the main tree, uncommitted until the driver's next commit). The dirty-park test runs the default fixture, so slice 2 starts beside slice 1 and lands during the park; what it pins is that slice 3, ready by then, does not spawn while slice 1's landing waits.
**Over:** the literal "porcelain empty", which no blocked slice can meet, and "slice 2 does not spawn", which a chained fixture makes true through the dependency alone, proving nothing about the park.
**Because:** both keep the intent: the pick leaves the main tree's code untouched, and nothing spawns while a landing waits.
**Undo:** tighten the asserts in `tests/commits.rs` (`a_conflicting_landing_blocks_the_slice_and_keeps_its_ref`, `a_dirty_path_in_the_main_tree_parks_the_landing_and_keeps_the_owners_edit`).

title: A test's owner file goes in after start
body: Preflight refuses a dirty main tree, so a test that dirties it (an owner's file) must write it after `factory run` returns, not before; `git restore` has no `--ignore-unmatch`.

title: What does a merging slice's respawn keep?
body:
**Chose:** a `building` slice whose `refs/factory/<NNN>/slice-NN` resolves and that holds a lane respawns as a merge worker on that lane as left: the ref is kept, the lane is not reset, and the pack gets an answer only when it came after the slice's last `landing_conflicted`. The third conflict's BLOCK also redoes the pick in the lane first, so the answer brings a merge worker on the conflict. A build spawn still deletes a stale ref (AD-8).
**Over:** AD-8 as is, which deletes the ref on every spawn, and handing every respawn the latest answer whatever its age.
**Because:** the merge worker resolves that commit and its landing reads its message; an answer from before the conflict is about the build already in the commit.
**Undo:** `spawn_on`'s `merge` flag and the `merging` test in the building loop in `src/scheduler.rs`.

title: A rate-limited merge worker keeps its lane
body:
**Chose:** a merge worker on a usage limit settles `rate_limited` and pauses the run, but the slice stays `building` on its lane, so the respawn after the reset is a merge worker on the half-resolved pick.
**Over:** today's build-worker path (`settle_limited`), which sets the slice `pending` and frees its lane.
**Because:** a freed lane is reset by the next slice that takes it, losing the pick, and a `pending` slice with a ref would respawn as a build worker.
**Undo:** call `settle_limited` from `route_merge`.

title: Two events for the merge, the conflict logged after the pick
body:
**Chose:** two new events, `merge_spawned { slice, attempt, session_id, pid }` and `landing_conflicted { slice, paths }`; the driver logs the second after the lane's reset and pick, and before the slice flips to `building`. A resumed driver that finds it after a worker's spawn settles that worker `done` (or `blocked`) and leaves the respawn to the building loop.
**Over:** reusing `slice_spawned` for merge workers, and logging the conflict before the pick.
**Because:** reports and the death count tell a merge worker by its event; an event after the pick means the lane is ready whenever it is seen.
**Undo:** fold `merge_spawned` into `slice_spawned` with a role field.

**Because:** both keep the intent: the two slices land in order, and the status board shows slice 02 `blocked`.
**Undo:** stop the run at slice 02's landing and assert HEAD~1..HEAD in `tests/merge.rs`.

title: Does a building slice respawn while a due checkpoint waits for a lane?
body:
**Chose:** while a checkpoint is due and no lane is free, the building loop still respawns a dead or limited `building` slice on its own lane; the respawn skip holds only when the checkpoint can take a lane.
**Over:** skipping every respawn while a checkpoint is due, as before this slice.
**Because:** with every lane held the checkpoint waits, so skipping the respawns too left nothing live and the run ended "nothing ready" in place of parking on the blocks or finishing the slice.
**Undo:** `checkpoint_waits` in the building loop of `src/scheduler.rs`; set it back to `board.checkpoint_due`.

title: What does a checkpoint worker's conflicting landing do?
body:
**Chose:** a checkpoint or fix worker whose lane commit conflicts on the feature tip commits the board files alone, writes a checkpoint block naming the paths and `refs/factory/<NNN>/checkpoint-n-<role>`, and parks. For the checkpoint worker the CP-n entry is already on the board, so once the owner answers, the run goes on without re-entering that checkpoint; the ref waits for the owner to cherry-pick.
**Over:** holding the checkpoint open until the ref lands.
**Because:** only the owner moves HEAD while a checkpoint runs, so a conflict is rare and is the owner's to resolve; the block's options name the cherry-pick, and the next spawn of that role deletes a stale ref.
**Undo:** `block_conflict` and `Landed::Conflict` in `src/checkpoint.rs`.

title: When does the main-tree-only test write needed.txt?

**Chose:** the main-tree-only test writes the untracked `needed.txt` right after `factory run` returns, before the first gate, in place of before `start`.
**Over:** writing it before `start`, as the slice's task 2 acceptance says.
**Because:** preflight refuses a dirty main tree, so the run would never start; the file is in the main tree for every gate run, which keeps the intent (the gate runs on HEAD, not on the main tree).
**Undo:** none needed unless preflight learns to ignore untracked files; then move the write before `start` in `a_file_only_the_main_tree_holds_does_not_turn_the_gate_green`.

title: What does a conflicting polish or CI fix landing do?
body:
**Chose:** a polish or CI fix lane commit that conflicts with the feature tip commits nothing, keeps `refs/factory/<NNN>/polish` (or `ci-fix-<round>`), writes a closeout block in phase `polish` (or `ci`) naming the paths and the ref, and parks. For polish, an answer of `proceed` after the owner cherry-picks the ref counts as polish done and the driver ships; any other answer spawns a fresh polish worker, whose spawn deletes the stale ref. For CI, the answer resumes the round as today.
**Over:** holding the closeout open until the ref lands, or a merge worker for closeout conflicts.
**Because:** nothing else is live in the closeout, so only the owner can move HEAD under a polish or CI fix worker; the conflict is rare and is theirs, as AD-15 settled for checkpoint workers.
**Undo:** `block_conflict` and `POLISH_CONFLICT` in `src/closeout.rs`, and the `polish_by_hand` test in `run()`.

title: What does a merge that leaves no marker do?
body:
**Chose:** a merge worker's exit blocks the slice, keeping `refs/factory/<NNN>/slice-NN`, in two more cases besides markers: a path the lane still holds unmerged with no marker to show it (a side deleted, a binary file), and a lane that, committed, changes nothing on its base. `contract-merge.md` now tells the worker to `git add`/`git rm` such a path. The pick in `start_merge` also errors when it fails and leaves no conflict.
**Over:** landing whatever `add -A` stages, which re-added a file the tip deleted, and deleting the ref and marking the slice `done` when the lane held nothing, which lost the slice when a respawn's lane had been reset.
**Because:** neither case can tell a resolution from lost work; the ref keeps the work and the block's options let the owner say. Pinned by two tests in `tests/merge.rs`.
**Undo:** `unmerged_paths`/`is_binary_conflict` and `block_empty_merge` in `src/scheduler.rs`, the new bullet in `assets/contract-merge.md`.

title: Does a failing driver settle a done slice's worker failed?
body:
**Chose:** a driver that fails while routing a worker, or abandons one that already exited, leaves that worker unsettled when its landing is still owed (the slice reads `done`, or its ref resolves); the resume's `settle_orphans` lands it, as after a kill.
**Over:** settling every such worker `failed`, as before.
**Because:** a `failed` row is never landed again, so a done slice's work stayed on its ref while the board said `done` and its dependents built without it.
**Undo:** `landing_owed` and its two calls (`reap`, `abandon`) in `src/scheduler.rs`.

title: Does the run go on while a recorded checkpoint's block is open?
body:
**Chose:** an open checkpoint-phase block holds the run even once its checkpoint is recorded: no ready slice spawns and the closeout does not start until it is answered; live workers run on. The conflict block's options now say "the run goes on past the recorded checkpoint" for the checkpoint role.
**Over:** going on at once, which AD-15's conflict block allowed by accident: CP-n is on the board, so the checkpoint was no longer due and nothing read the block.
**Because:** the block asks the owner to cherry-pick the worker's ref; a run that moves on lands slices on a tip the owner is about to change.
**Undo:** `checkpoint_block` in the drive loop of `src/scheduler.rs`, and the `next` wording in `checkpoint::block_conflict`.

title: Which paths does a landing write and check?
body:
**Chose:** `land` reads the paths the pick writes off the merged tree (`git merge-tree` before the dirty check), counts an ignored file at one of them as dirty, undoes the pick when its commit fails, runs git with `GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1`, and `commit_lane` detaches the lane's HEAD before `reset --soft`.
**Over:** the lane commit's own paths, ignored files left out of the dirty check, no rollback, glob pathspecs, and a reset on whatever branch the worker switched to.
**Because:** each was a way to lose or mix up work: a tip rename made `commit -- old.txt` fail mid-pick, a hook failure left the main tree half-picked, an owner's ignored file was overwritten, `[a].txt` committed the owner's `a.txt`, and a worker's branch moved. Pinned by five tests in `src/land.rs`.
**Undo:** the matching hunks in `src/land.rs`.
